summary: Glacier Wall frame cabin built 1945, about two miles east of Heavens Peak per firelookout.com (FFLA coordinates put it about four miles from the standing lookout; unresolved), destroyed 1963 per firelookout.com; no source consulted describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1963 per firelookout.com; no source consulted describes what remains at the site.
facts.location: within Glacier National Park, Flathead County, Montana; about six miles west of Logan Pass

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both sites carry the Heavens Peak name and 1945 build dates. firelookout.com describes #1 as a 15-by-17-foot frame cabin about two miles east, and the FFLA list keeps the two as separate entries, so the story treats them as different structures.

unresolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com places #1 about two miles east of Heavens Peak. The FFLA coordinates for #1 (48.70230, -113.82340) and for the standing lookout (48.74882, -113.87616) are about 4.0 miles apart by great-circle distance (computed). No source consulted resolves which is right; the story discloses the mismatch and does not pick one.

sources.title: Montana Lookouts, Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: The 1945 build, the 15-by-17-foot size and the 1963 destruction date come only from firelookout.com; FFLA confirms only that the site is gone. Web searches and the NRHP nomination text turned up no mention of a #1 structure or the 1963 date. Location conflict (see unresolved_conflicts): firelookout.com says about two miles east of Heavens Peak; the FFLA coordinates put #1 about 4.0 miles (6.5 km) from the FFLA point for the standing lookout. The story now discloses this and states that the location is unresolved; check which is right before relying on either distance. Backcountry site inside Glacier National Park; access is not described in any source, and nothing here encourages a visit.
